blocks.es_reference: "'Grandes y maravillosas son tus obras, Señor Dios Todopoderoso; justos y verdaderos son tus caminos, Rey de los santos.'... Y salió una gran voz del templo del cielo, del trono, diciendo: 'Hecho está.'" — Apocalipsis 15:3; 16:17 (RVG)

blocks.en: The Lamb and the 144,000 on Mount Zion
blocks.es_reference: El Cordero y los Ciento Cuarenta y Cuatro Mil en el Monte de Sión

blocks.en: After the dark vision of the dragon and the two beasts, chapter fourteen opens with a scene of comfort. "Then I looked, and behold, a Lamb standing on Mount Zion, and with Him one hundred and forty-four thousand, having His Father's name written on their foreheads" (Revelation 14:1). Set against those who took the mark of the beast on their foreheads, here are the redeemed, sealed instead with the name of God, standing secure with the Lamb. They sing a new song that no one else can learn, for they alone have been "redeemed from the earth" (Revelation 14:3). They are called firstfruits to God and to the Lamb, they follow the Lamb wherever He goes, and no lie is found in their mouths. The 144,000 are the people of God, and as in chapter seven their number and identity have been understood in more than one way, which the course has already presented fairly. What matters here is the contrast: while the world bears the mark of the beast and faces wrath, the Lamb's own bear the Father's name and stand safe with Him on Mount Zion.
blocks.es_reference: Después de la oscura visión del dragón y las dos bestias, el capítulo catorce abre con una escena de consuelo. "Y miré, y he aquí un Cordero estaba en pie sobre el monte de Sión, y con él ciento cuarenta y cuatro mil, que tenían el nombre de su Padre escrito en sus frentes" (Apocalipsis 14:1). Frente a los que tomaron la marca de la bestia en sus frentes, aquí están los redimidos, sellados en cambio con el nombre de Dios, en pie seguros con el Cordero. Cantan un cántico nuevo que ningún otro puede aprender, pues solo ellos han sido "redimidos de la tierra" (Apocalipsis 14:3). Son llamados primicias para Dios y para el Cordero, siguen al Cordero por dondequiera que va, y no se halla mentira en sus bocas. Los ciento cuarenta y cuatro mil son el pueblo de Dios, y como en el capítulo siete su número e identidad se han entendido de más de una manera, lo cual el curso ya ha presentado con justicia. Lo que importa aquí es el contraste: mientras el mundo lleva la marca de la bestia y enfrenta la ira, los del Cordero llevan el nombre del Padre y están seguros con él sobre el monte de Sión.

blocks.en: The Three Angels: Gospel, Babylon, and Warning
blocks.es_reference: Los Tres Ángeles: Evangelio, Babilonia, y Advertencia

blocks.en: Then three angels fly through the heavens with three announcements. The first has "the everlasting gospel to preach to those who dwell on the earth, to every nation, tribe, tongue, and people," crying, "Fear God and give glory to Him, for the hour of His judgment has come; and worship Him who made heaven and earth" (Revelation 14:6-7). Even in the hour of judgment, the gospel still calls all nations to turn to God. The second angel announces, "Babylon is fallen, is fallen, that great city" (Revelation 14:8), the first mention of the doomed world-city that chapters seventeen and eighteen will describe. The third angel gives a solemn warning: whoever worships the beast and receives its mark "shall also drink of the wine of the wrath of God" and be tormented with fire (Revelation 14:9-11). Then comes a word for the church: "Here is the patience of the saints; here are those who keep the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus" (Revelation 14:12), and a blessing from heaven, "Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord from now on... that they may rest from their labors, and their works follow them" (Revelation 14:13).
blocks.es_reference: Luego tres ángeles vuelan por los cielos con tres anuncios. El primero tiene "el evangelio eterno para predicarlo a los moradores de la tierra, y a toda nación, tribu, lengua y pueblo," clamando: "Temed a Dios, y dadle gloria, porque la hora de su juicio ha venido; y adorad a aquel que hizo el cielo y la tierra" (Apocalipsis 14:6-7). Aun en la hora del juicio, el evangelio todavía llama a todas las naciones a volverse a Dios. El segundo ángel anuncia: "Ha caído, ha caído Babilonia, aquella gran ciudad" (Apocalipsis 14:8), la primera mención de la condenada ciudad del mundo que los capítulos diecisiete y dieciocho describirán. El tercer ángel da una solemne advertencia: quien adora a la bestia y recibe su marca "también beberá del vino de la ira de Dios" y será atormentado con fuego (Apocalipsis 14:9-11). Entonces viene una palabra para la iglesia: "Aquí está la paciencia de los santos; aquí están los que guardan los mandamientos de Dios y la fe de Jesús" (Apocalipsis 14:12), y una bienaventuranza del cielo: "Bienaventurados los muertos que de aquí en adelante mueren en el Señor... descansarán de sus trabajos; y sus obras con ellos siguen" (Apocalipsis 14:13).

blocks.en: The Two Harvests of the Earth
blocks.es_reference: Las Dos Cosechas de la Tierra

blocks.en: The chapter closes with two harvests. First, John sees One like the Son of Man seated on a white cloud, with a golden crown and a sharp sickle, and an angel cries, "Thrust in Your sickle and reap, for the time has come for You to reap, for the harvest of the earth is ripe" (Revelation 14:15), and the earth is reaped. Some understand this grain harvest as the gathering of the redeemed and others as a harvest of judgment, and the course leaves the question open. Then comes a second, plainly fearful harvest: another angel with a sharp sickle gathers the grapes of the earth and throws them "into the great winepress of the wrath of God" (Revelation 14:19). The winepress is trodden outside the city, and blood flows from it as high as the horses' bridles for a great distance. It is a terrible picture of the judgment of God upon a ripened, rebellious world, and it sets the stage for the seven bowls of wrath that follow.
blocks.es_reference: El capítulo cierra con dos cosechas. Primero, Juan ve uno semejante al Hijo del Hombre sentado sobre una nube blanca, con una corona de oro y una hoz aguda, y un ángel clama: "Mete tu hoz, y siega; porque la hora de segar te ha venido, porque la mies de la tierra está madura" (Apocalipsis 14:15), y la tierra es segada. Algunos entienden esta siega de grano como la reunión de los redimidos y otros como una siega de juicio, y el curso deja la pregunta abierta. Luego viene una segunda cosecha, claramente temible: otro ángel con una hoz aguda vendimia las uvas de la tierra y las echa "en el gran lagar de la ira de Dios" (Apocalipsis 14:19). El lagar es pisado fuera de la ciudad, y sale de él sangre hasta los frenos de los caballos por una gran distancia. Es una imagen terrible del juicio de Dios sobre un mundo maduro y rebelde, y prepara el escenario para las siete copas de ira que siguen.

blocks.en: The Song of Moses and the Lamb
blocks.es_reference: El Cántico de Moisés y del Cordero

blocks.en: Chapter fifteen is a short but solemn prelude to the final plagues. John sees another sign in heaven, "seven angels having the seven last plagues, for in them the wrath of God is complete" (Revelation 15:1). Before they are poured out, he sees those who had gained the victory over the beast and its image, standing on a sea of glass mingled with fire, holding harps of God. They sing "the song of Moses, the servant of God, and the song of the Lamb" (Revelation 15:3), joining the great deliverance at the Red Sea to the greater deliverance won by the Lamb. Their song is pure praise of God's justice: "Great and marvelous are Your works, Lord God Almighty! Just and true are Your ways, O King of the saints! Who shall not fear You, O Lord, and glorify Your name?... For all nations shall come and worship before You, for Your judgments have been manifested" (Revelation 15:3-4). The victors do not gloat over the wrath to come; they worship God because His judgments are right.
blocks.es_reference: El capítulo quince es un breve pero solemne preludio a las plagas finales. Juan ve otra señal en el cielo, "siete ángeles que tenían las siete plagas postreras; porque en ellas es consumada la ira de Dios" (Apocalipsis 15:1). Antes de que sean derramadas, ve a los que habían alcanzado la victoria sobre la bestia y su imagen, en pie sobre un mar de vidrio mezclado con fuego, teniendo las arpas de Dios. Cantan "el cántico de Moisés, siervo de Dios, y el cántico del Cordero" (Apocalipsis 15:3), uniendo la gran liberación en el Mar Rojo a la mayor liberación ganada por el Cordero. Su cántico es pura alabanza de la justicia de Dios: "Grandes y maravillosas son tus obras, Señor Dios Todopoderoso; justos y verdaderos son tus caminos, Rey de los santos. ¿Quién no te temerá, oh Señor, y glorificará tu nombre?... porque todas las naciones vendrán y adorarán delante de ti, porque tus juicios se han manifestado" (Apocalipsis 15:3-4). Los vencedores no se jactan de la ira por venir; adoran a Dios porque sus juicios son justos.

blocks.en: The Temple Filled with Glory
blocks.es_reference: El Templo Lleno de Gloria

blocks.en: Then the heavenly sanctuary is opened: "the temple of the tabernacle of the testimony in heaven was opened" (Revelation 15:5), and out of it come the seven angels with the seven plagues, clothed in pure bright linen with golden bands. One of the four living creatures gives them "seven golden bowls full of the wrath of God who lives forever and ever" (Revelation 15:7). The wrath of God is now gathered into bowls, ready to be poured out in full. Finally "the temple was filled with smoke from the glory of God and from His power, and no one was able to enter the temple till the seven plagues of the seven angels were completed" (Revelation 15:8). The smoke of God's glory bars the way, a sign that the time for intercession has passed and the final judgments must now run their course. Everything is solemn, ordered, and under the hand of the holy God whose wrath is about to be completed.
blocks.es_reference: Entonces el santuario celestial es abierto: "el templo del tabernáculo del testimonio en el cielo fue abierto" (Apocalipsis 15:5), y de él salen los siete ángeles con las siete plagas, vestidos de lino limpio y resplandeciente con cintos de oro. Uno de los cuatro animales les da "siete copas de oro, llenas de la ira de Dios, que vive por los siglos de los siglos" (Apocalipsis 15:7). La ira de Dios está ahora reunida en copas, lista para ser derramada por completo. Finalmente "el templo se llenó de humo por la gloria de Dios, y por su poder; y ninguno podía entrar en el templo, hasta que fuesen consumadas las siete plagas de los siete ángeles" (Apocalipsis 15:8). El humo de la gloria de Dios cierra el paso, una señal de que el tiempo de la intercesión ha pasado y los juicios finales deben ahora seguir su curso. Todo es solemne, ordenado, y bajo la mano del Dios santo cuya ira está por ser consumada.

blocks.en: The Seven Bowls of Wrath
blocks.es_reference: Las Siete Copas de Ira

blocks.en: A loud voice from the temple commands, "Go and pour out the bowls of the wrath of God on the earth" (Revelation 16:1). The first bowl brings foul, loathsome sores on those who bear the mark of the beast and worship its image. The second turns the sea to blood like a dead man's, and every living thing in it dies. The third turns the rivers and springs to blood. The fourth gives the sun power to scorch men with fire. The fifth plunges the throne of the beast and its kingdom into darkness, so that men gnaw their tongues in pain. The sixth dries up the great river Euphrates to prepare the way for the kings from the East, and three unclean spirits like frogs come out of the mouths of the dragon, the beast, and the false prophet, going out to gather the kings of the world "to the battle of that great day of God Almighty" at a place called Armageddon (Revelation 16:13-16). Two things stand out. First, unlike the trumpets, which struck only a third, the bowls fall in full: this is the complete, unmixed wrath of God. Second, again and again the hardened do not repent but only blaspheme God, showing once more that judgment alone cannot turn a rebel heart.
blocks.es_reference: Una gran voz del templo manda: "Id, y derramad las siete copas de la ira de Dios sobre la tierra" (Apocalipsis 16:1). La primera copa trae una úlcera maligna y pestilente sobre los que llevan la marca de la bestia y adoran su imagen. La segunda convierte el mar en sangre como de un muerto, y todo ser vivo en él muere. La tercera convierte los ríos y las fuentes en sangre. La cuarta da al sol poder para quemar a los hombres con fuego. La quinta sume el trono de la bestia y su reino en tinieblas, de modo que los hombres muerden sus lenguas de dolor. La sexta seca el gran río Éufrates para preparar el camino de los reyes del oriente, y tres espíritus inmundos a manera de ranas salen de las bocas del dragón, la bestia, y el falso profeta, saliendo a reunir a los reyes del mundo "a la batalla de aquel gran día del Dios Todopoderoso" en un lugar llamado Armagedón (Apocalipsis 16:13-16). Dos cosas resaltan. Primero, a diferencia de las trompetas, que golpeaban solo una tercera parte, las copas caen por completo: esta es la ira completa y sin mezcla de Dios. Segundo, una y otra vez los endurecidos no se arrepienten sino que solo blasfeman a Dios, mostrando de nuevo que el juicio por sí solo no puede volver un corazón rebelde.

blocks.en: "It Is Done!" and the Justice of God
blocks.es_reference: "Hecho Está" y la Justicia de Dios

blocks.en: Twice in chapter sixteen the justice of God is openly declared. When the rivers become blood, the angel of the waters says, "You are righteous, O Lord... because You have judged these things. For they have shed the blood of saints and prophets, and You have given them blood to drink. For it is their just due" (Revelation 16:5-6), and the altar answers, "Even so, Lord God Almighty, true and righteous are Your judgments" (Revelation 16:7). The wrath of God is never arbitrary; it repays the blood of His martyred people, and it is just. Then the seventh angel pours out his bowl into the air, and a loud voice from the throne cries, "It is done!" (Revelation 16:17). There follow the greatest earthquake the world has ever known, the splitting of the great city into three parts, and the remembering of Babylon to give her the cup of God's fury, with islands and mountains fleeing and great hailstones falling, while men still blaspheme God. With "It is done," the wrath of God reaches its completion, and the way is opened for the fall of Babylon and the return of Christ. So chapters fourteen through sixteen set the redeemed, secure with the Lamb, over against the followers of the beast under wrath; they sound both the gospel and the warning; they vindicate the justice of God; and they bring His wrath to its appointed end. The call to the church is plain: keep the faith of Jesus, share in the patience of the saints, and be found among the Lamb's own, whose names are written in His book.
blocks.es_reference: Dos veces en el capítulo dieciséis se declara abiertamente la justicia de Dios. Cuando los ríos se vuelven sangre, el ángel de las aguas dice: "Justo eres tú, oh Señor... porque has juzgado estas cosas. Por cuanto derramaron la sangre de los santos y de los profetas, también tú les has dado a beber sangre; pues lo merecen" (Apocalipsis 16:5-6), y el altar responde: "Ciertamente, Señor Dios Todopoderoso, tus juicios son verdaderos y justos" (Apocalipsis 16:7). La ira de Dios nunca es arbitraria; paga la sangre de su pueblo martirizado, y es justa. Entonces el séptimo ángel derrama su copa por el aire, y una gran voz del trono clama: "Hecho está" (Apocalipsis 16:17). Siguen el mayor terremoto que el mundo ha conocido jamás, la división de la gran ciudad en tres partes, y el recuerdo de Babilonia para darle el cáliz del furor de la ira de Dios, con islas y montes que huyen y grandes granizos que caen, mientras los hombres aún blasfeman a Dios. Con "Hecho está," la ira de Dios llega a su consumación, y se abre el camino para la caída de Babilonia y la venida de Cristo. Así los capítulos catorce al dieciséis ponen a los redimidos, seguros con el Cordero, frente a los seguidores de la bestia bajo la ira; suenan tanto el evangelio como la advertencia; vindican la justicia de Dios; y llevan su ira a su fin señalado. El llamado a la iglesia es claro: guardar la fe de Jesús, compartir en la paciencia de los santos, y ser hallados entre los del Cordero, cuyos nombres están escritos en su libro.

options: Firstfruits to God and the Lamb, who follow Him wherever He goes
mc.why: They are firstfruits to God and follow the Lamb wherever He goes (14:4).

options: The everlasting gospel: fear God, for the hour of His judgment has come
The names in the Book of Life

options: The wrath of God is completed

options: The whole — the complete, unmixed wrath of God
mc.why: The bowls fall in full, the complete wrath of God (16; cf. 15:1).

mc.why: Foul, loathsome sores fell on those who bore the beast's mark (16:2).

options: Righteous, repaying those who shed the blood of saints
mc.why: "You are righteous... they have shed the blood of saints, and You have given them blood to drink" (16:5-6).

mc.why: The Euphrates was dried up for the kings from the East (16:12).

mc.stem: Three unclean spirits like frogs, from the dragon, beast, and false prophet, gathered the kings of the world to a place called:
mc.why: They gathered the kings to the battle at Armageddon (16:13-16).

mc.stem: When the seventh bowl was poured out, a loud voice from the throne said:
mc.why: "It is done!" — the wrath of God reaches completion (16:17).

mc.stem: The central message of chapters 14-16 is that:
options: God's wrath is just and complete, while the redeemed are secure with the Lamb

sa.prompt: Describe the Lamb and the 144,000 on Mount Zion (14:1-5) and the contrast with the followers of the beast.
sa.model: After the dark vision of the dragon and the beasts, chapter fourteen opens with comfort. John sees the Lamb standing on Mount Zion, and with Him the hundred and forty-four thousand, who have the Father's name written on their foreheads. The contrast is deliberate and striking: while the world bears the mark of the beast on its forehead, these bear the name of God and stand secure with the Lamb. They sing a new song that no one else can learn, for they alone have been redeemed from the earth. They are called firstfruits to God and to the Lamb, they follow the Lamb wherever He goes, and no lie is found in their mouths. The 144,000 are the people of God, and as in chapter seven their number and identity have been understood in more than one way, which the course has already presented fairly. What matters here is the comfort the scene gives: over against the doomed followers of the beast, the redeemed of the Lamb are sealed with the Father's name and kept safe with Him, the firstfruits of His harvest.

sa.prompt: Describe the message of the three angels in Revelation 14:6-13.
sa.model: Three angels fly through the heavens with three announcements. The first carries the everlasting gospel to preach to those who dwell on the earth, to every nation, tribe, tongue, and people, crying, fear God and give Him glory, for the hour of His judgment has come, and worship Him who made heaven and earth. Even in the hour of judgment the gospel still calls all nations to turn to God. The second angel announces that Babylon is fallen, that great city, the first mention of the doomed world-city that later chapters will describe. The third angel gives a solemn warning, that whoever worships the beast and receives its mark will drink the wine of the wrath of God and be tormented. Then comes a word for the church: here is the patience of the saints, those who keep the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus. And a voice from heaven adds a blessing, blessed are the dead who die in the Lord, for they rest from their labors and their works follow them. So the three angels hold together gospel, the doom of the world-system, and warning, while comforting the faithful.

sa.prompt: Describe the two harvests of the earth in Revelation 14:14-20.
sa.model: The chapter closes with two harvests. First John sees One like the Son of Man seated on a white cloud, with a golden crown and a sharp sickle, and an angel cries to thrust in the sickle and reap, for the harvest of the earth is ripe, and the earth is reaped. Some understand this grain harvest as the gathering of the redeemed and others as a harvest of judgment, and the course leaves the question open. Then comes a second and plainly fearful harvest: another angel with a sharp sickle gathers the grapes of the earth and throws them into the great winepress of the wrath of God. The winepress is trodden outside the city, and blood flows from it as high as the horses' bridles for a great distance. This vintage is a terrible picture of the judgment of God upon a ripened, rebellious world that has refused Him. The double image of grain and grapes shows both the gathering and the judgment that the end will bring, and it sets the stage for the seven bowls of wrath that follow in the next chapters.

sa.prompt: Describe the song of Moses and of the Lamb in Revelation 15:1-4.
sa.model: Chapter fifteen is a short but solemn prelude to the final plagues. John sees another sign in heaven, seven angels having the seven last plagues, for in them the wrath of God is complete. Before they are poured out, he sees those who had gained the victory over the beast and its image, standing on a sea of glass mingled with fire and holding harps of God. They sing the song of Moses the servant of God and the song of the Lamb, joining the great deliverance at the Red Sea to the greater deliverance won by the Lamb. Their song is pure praise of God's justice: great and marvelous are Your works, Lord God Almighty, just and true are Your ways, O King of the saints, and they ask who shall not fear and glorify His name, for all nations will come and worship before Him, because His judgments have been manifested. The victors do not gloat over the wrath that is coming; instead they worship God precisely because His judgments are just and true, and they look forward to the nations coming to worship Him.

sa.prompt: Describe the seven angels and the temple filled with glory in Revelation 15:5-8.
sa.model: Then the heavenly sanctuary is opened, the temple of the tabernacle of the testimony in heaven, and out of it come the seven angels with the seven plagues, clothed in pure bright linen with golden bands across their chests. One of the four living creatures gives them seven golden bowls full of the wrath of God who lives forever and ever, so that the wrath of God is now gathered into bowls, ready to be poured out in full. Finally the temple is filled with smoke from the glory of God and from His power, and no one is able to enter the temple until the seven plagues of the seven angels are completed. The smoke of God's glory bars the way into the temple, a solemn sign that the time for intercession has passed and the final judgments must now run their course without interruption. Everything in the scene is ordered, holy, and under the hand of the eternal God. The vision impresses on the reader that the bowls about to fall are not random fury but the deliberate, completed wrath of the holy God, carried out by His angels from His own temple.

sa.prompt: Describe the seven bowls of wrath in Revelation 16:1-16 and how they differ from the trumpets.
sa.model: A loud voice from the temple commands the angels to pour out the bowls of the wrath of God on the earth. The first bowl brings foul, loathsome sores on those who bear the mark of the beast and worship its image. The second turns the sea to blood like a dead man's, and every living thing in it dies. The third turns the rivers and springs to blood. The fourth gives the sun power to scorch men with fire. The fifth plunges the throne of the beast and its kingdom into darkness, so that men gnaw their tongues in pain. The sixth dries up the great river Euphrates to prepare the way for the kings from the East, and three unclean spirits like frogs come from the mouths of the dragon, the beast, and the false prophet to gather the kings of the world to the battle at Armageddon. Two things differ from the trumpets. First, the trumpets struck only a third, but the bowls fall in full, the complete and unmixed wrath of God. Second, again and again the hardened do not repent but only blaspheme God, showing once more that judgment by itself cannot turn a rebel heart.

sa.prompt: How does Revelation 16 affirm the justice of God in His judgments?
sa.model: Twice in chapter sixteen the justice of God is openly declared, so that no reader may think His wrath unfair. When the rivers become blood, the angel of the waters says, You are righteous, O Lord, because You have judged these things, for they have shed the blood of saints and prophets, and You have given them blood to drink, for it is their just due. The punishment fits the crime: those who shed the blood of God's people are given blood in return. Then the altar itself answers, even so, Lord God Almighty, true and righteous are Your judgments. The wrath of God is never arbitrary or cruel; it repays the blood of His martyred saints and prophets, and it is just. This is a great comfort to a suffering church, for it means that the cry of the martyrs under the altar, how long until You avenge our blood, is answered righteously. God does judge, but His judgments are measured, deserved, and true, and even the instruments of His wrath confess that what He does is right.

sa.prompt: What happens at the seventh bowl, and what does the cry "It is done!" mean?
sa.model: The seventh angel pours out his bowl into the air, and a loud voice comes out of the temple from the throne, crying, It is done. With that cry the wrath of God reaches its completion. There follow the greatest earthquake the world has ever known, so great that the great city is split into three parts, and Babylon is remembered before God to be given the cup of the wine of the fierceness of His wrath. Islands flee away and the mountains are not found, and great hailstones, each about the weight of a talent, fall upon men, who still only blaspheme God because of the plague of the hail. The words it is done mark the end of the bowls and the completion of the wrath of God, just as a later cry will mark the completion of all things. The way is now opened for the fall of Babylon, which the next chapters describe in detail, and beyond that for the return of Christ. So the seventh bowl does not merely add another plague but brings the judgments of wrath to their appointed end, declaring that God's purpose in judgment is finished.

sa.prompt: What do chapters 14-16 reveal about the contrast between the redeemed and the followers of the beast?
sa.model: Chapters fourteen through sixteen draw a sharp contrast between two groups. On one side are the redeemed, the hundred and forty-four thousand who stand with the Lamb on Mount Zion, sealed with the Father's name on their foreheads, singing a new song, following the Lamb wherever He goes, kept secure as the firstfruits of God. The dead who die in the Lord are called blessed, for they rest from their labors. On the other side are the followers of the beast, who bear its mark on their foreheads and worship its image. These drink the wine of the wrath of God, suffer the loathsome sores and the plagues of the bowls, and even under judgment refuse to repent and only blaspheme God. The dividing line is the same one drawn in chapter thirteen: whose name is written in the Lamb's book, and whose forehead bears the name of God rather than the mark of the beast. So the vision both warns and comforts. It warns that the followers of the beast face the complete wrath of God, and it comforts the church that the Lamb's own are sealed, secure, and blessed.

sa.prompt: Summarize the central truth of Unit 9: what do chapters 14-16 teach the church?
sa.model: The central truth of Unit 9 is that the wrath of God against evil is both just and complete, while the redeemed are kept safe with the Lamb. Chapters fourteen through sixteen set the redeemed, who stand with the Lamb on Mount Zion sealed with the Father's name, over against the followers of the beast, who bear its mark and face judgment. They sound both the gospel, which still calls every nation to fear God, and the warning against worshiping the beast. They vindicate the justice of God, for His judgments repay the blood of His saints and are confessed to be true and righteous. And they bring the wrath of God to its appointed end, so that at the seventh bowl a voice from the throne cries, it is done, opening the way for the fall of Babylon and the coming of Christ. Through it all the hardened do not repent but only blaspheme, while the faithful are called to the patience of the saints and the faith of Jesus. The church is summoned to be found among the Lamb's own, sealed with His name, rather than among those who bear the mark of the beast.
